mainTopic: The source for permitting a fetus through its mother's שחיטה, and when a בכור becomes holy during birth
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of which פסוק permits a fetus found inside a slaughtered animal. Under the "hoof" reading, a dove-shaped fetus is forbidden because it has no hooves. A fetus with uncloven hooves is still permitted, because דבי רבי ישמעאל reads "פרסה" as enough by itself. רב שימי בר אשי instead keeps the first source, "בהמה בבהמה". He explains that the משנה forbidding תמורה of fetuses follows רבי שמעון, who compares תמורה to מעשר בהמה. The גמרא tries to prove this attribution from רבי יוסי's argument and a ברייתא about declaring an animal's leg an עולה. It then rejects the proof, since רבי יוסי may only be explaining his own view. A new משנה teaches that a firstborn stuck during birth may be cut up and thrown to the dogs, but once most of it is out it is holy and must be buried. רב הונא holds that a בכור's holiness works backwards (למפרע), and רבה holds that it starts only once most of it is out (מכאן ולהבא). They apply these views to a partial sale to a גוי and to a birth that was partly through the side wall. The גמרא then begins explaining why both cases are needed.

steps.title: A dove-shaped fetus is forbidden because it has no hooves
steps.stepSummary: Under the reading that ties the permit to "פרסה", a fetus must have hooves, and a dove-shaped fetus does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: I need hooves, and this one has none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, under this reading of the פסוק, a fetus shaped like a dove stays forbidden even though it was inside a slaughtered animal: the פסוק requires hooves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fetus is permitted through the word "פרסה" (hoof) in the פסוק. A fetus with no hooves, like one shaped like a bird, does not meet that condition. So it gets no permit from its mother's שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hooves
I require, I need
There is none, it is missing

phrases.english: I require hooves, and there are none.
phrases.notes: He is talking about a fetus shaped like a dove, which the גמרא was discussing just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about which פסוק permits the fetus, applying the "hooves" reading to a dove-shaped fetus.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the condition the פסוק requires
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think any fetus found inside a slaughtered animal is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under this reading, only a fetus with hooves is permitted; a dove-shaped fetus is not.

steps.title: Then a fetus with uncloven hooves should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: If hooves are required as the פסוק describes them (split hooves), a fetus with solid, uncloven hooves inside a cow should be forbidden, yet we know it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a fetus with uncloven hooves found inside a cow should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the "hooves" reading. If the fetus must match the פסוק's description, one with uncloven hooves should be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק speaks of split hooves ("שוסעת שסע"). A קלוט has hooves that are not split. If the permit depends on the פסוק's signs, a קלוט fetus should fail. But an earlier ברייתא permits it, so the reading seems to clash with that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, now that you said this; introduces a challenge
An animal with solid, uncloven hooves
Inside a cow's womb

phrases.english: But if that is so,
a fetus with uncloven hooves inside a cow should be forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, קָלוּט בִּמְעֵי פָּרָה לִיתְּסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the "hooves" requirement just stated in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the fetus's permit depends on the hooves described in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק describes split hooves. A קלוט fetus lacks them, so it should be forbidden, against the known ruling that it is permitted.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads "a hoof" on its own
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל, following רבי שמעון בן יוחי, reads the פסוק as "פרסה בבהמה תאכלו". Any hoof is enough, even an uncloven one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught, like רבי שמעון בן יוחי: "A hoof, in the animal, you may eat."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word "פרסה" stands on its own, so even an uncloven hoof counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed hooves must be split. Here the word "פרסה" is read apart from "split into two hooves". So any hoof qualifies. That keeps the קלוט fetus permitted and still forbids the dove-shaped one.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
"A hoof, in the animal, you may eat"; the פסוק read so that a hoof alone is enough

steps.whatToRemember: Under the "hoof" reading, any hoof (even uncloven) is enough. Only a fetus with no hooves at all, like a dove-shaped one, is left out.

phrases.english: This is as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught
in accordance with רבי שמעון בן יוחי:
"A hoof, in the animal, you may eat."
phrases.notes: This is not one continuous פסוק. It picks out words from דברים 14:6, reading "hoof" as a condition all by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so that each word is its own condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Hooves must be split, as the full פסוק describes, so a קלוט fetus fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: "פרסה" alone is enough, so any hoof qualifies and the קלוט fetus is permitted.

steps.title: רב שימי בר אשי keeps the first source and says the תמורה משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי goes back to the original source for the fetus's permit. He answers the problem from "אין ממירין" by saying that משנה is רבי שמעון's view, and he compares תמורה to מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: Really, it is as you said at first. As for your difficulty from "one cannot substitute": whose view is that? It is רבי שמעון, who compares substitution to the animal tithe. Just as the tithe does not apply to limbs and fetuses, so too substitution does not apply to limbs and fetuses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי offers a different solution. He keeps the original source and explains that the troubling משנה in תמורה follows רבי שמעון's special reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source ("בהמה בבהמה") calls the fetus a "בהמה", an animal in its own right. That seemed to clash with the משנה saying you cannot substitute a fetus, since תמורה applies to a בהמה. רב שימי says that משנה is רבי שמעון. In his view תמורה works like מעשר, and מעשר applies only to whole, walking animals. So fetuses are left out because of this comparison, not because they are not a בהמה, and the original source can stay.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; going back to an earlier position
One cannot make a substitution (תמורה)
Whose view is this?
Compares two laws so they share the same rules (הקש)
Substituting an ordinary animal for a קרבן, which makes both holy
Here, the animal tithe (מעשר בהמה)

steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי is not saying a fetus is not a בהמה. He is saying the rule against substituting it comes from רבי שמעון's comparison of תמורה to מעשר, which only applies to animals that can walk under the rod. It is a special exception, not proof against the original source.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the original source ("בהמה בבהמה") by moving the conflicting משנה to one תנא's special reasoning.

phrases.english: רב שימי בר אשי said:
Actually, it is as you said originally,
phrases.notes: He means the first source for the fetus's permit, from earlier in the סוגיא, before the "hoof" reading.

phrases.english: and as for what was difficult for you, "one cannot substitute,"
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in תמורה saying you cannot substitute limbs or fetuses.

phrases.english: whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון,
who compares substitution to the tithe:
just as the tithe does not apply
to limbs and fetuses,
so too substitution does not apply
to limbs and fetuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם כִּדְקָאָמְרַתְּ מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the "hoof" reading of steps 1-3 and returns to the original source with a new answer to its difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the conflicting משנה to a specific תנא (הא מני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה "אין ממירין" is everyone's view and shows the fetus is not treated as a full בהמה, so the original source "בהמה בבהמה" fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי שמעון, who compares תמורה to מעשר; so the original source still stands.

steps.title: How do we know that משנה is רבי שמעון's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the משנה "אין ממירין" follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know the anonymous משנה in תמורה is רבי שמעון's view. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי's answer depends on naming the משנה's author. The גמרא wants a source showing that this naming is right, not just guessed.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? A request for proof

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for the attribution made in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the משנה "אין ממירין" follows רבי שמעון

steps.title: רבי יוסי says naming a leg for תמורה makes the whole animal a substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יוסי's statement from that משנה. Just as declaring an animal's leg an עולה makes the whole animal an עולה, saying a leg is a substitute makes the whole animal a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי יוסי said, "With consecrated animals, one who says 'the leg of this one is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה. So too, when he says 'the leg of this one is in place of that one', the whole animal should be a substitute in its place."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its proof by quoting רבי יוסי from the same משנה. He holds that a limb can trigger תמורה for the whole animal. This sets up the argument the גמרא will finish next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי argues from regular הקדש. Making one leg holy spreads to the whole animal, and he says תמורה should work the same way. This shows that in this משנה, רבי יוסי disagrees with the rule that תמורה does not work on limbs. That disagreement helps show who holds the other opinion in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so? Introduces a comparison or argument
Consecrated animals, קרבנות
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
In place of this one; the wording used for תמורה

phrases.english: As we learned: רבי יוסי said:
But with regard to consecrated animals,
one who says, "The leg of this one is an עולה"
the whole animal is an עולה;

phrases.aramaic: אַף כְּשֶׁיֹּאמַר: ״רֶגֶל שֶׁל זוֹ תַּחַת זוֹ״
phrases.english: so too when he says, "The leg of this one is in place of that one,"
the whole animal should be a substitute in its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 5 by quoting the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה "אין ממירין" follows רבי שמעון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תמורה, where רבי יוסי says tying תמורה to a limb takes effect on the whole animal

steps.title: Who is רבי יוסי arguing with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whom רבי יוסי is answering. It first suggests רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, then questions whether they even hold the reasoning about an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom is רבי יוסי answering? If you say he is answering רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, do they even agree with this idea?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the other side is in רבי יוסי's argument. This sets up the next move, a ברייתא that shows what רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's argument only works against someone who already agrees that declaring a leg an עולה makes the whole animal an עולה. So the גמרא checks who agrees with that idea. If רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not agree with it, he cannot be arguing with them.

keyTerms.meaning: answering him, arguing back against him
a line of reasoning, an idea someone holds

phrases.english: To whom is he responding?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוסי, from his statement in the last step: 'just as with an עולה, so too with תמורה.'

phrases.english: If you say to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
do they hold this reasoning?
phrases.notes: 'This reasoning' means the idea that saying 'its leg is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out the proof from רבי יוסי's statement in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the other side that רבי יוסי argues against with his comparison to an עולה?

steps.title: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say only the leg becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold that declaring a leg an עולה makes only that leg holy, not the whole animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that if a person says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה,' the whole animal becomes an עולה. The פסוק says 'of it,' so part of it is holy and not all of it. One might think the leg can become non-holy again. The פסוק says 'it shall be,' so it stays holy. So what happens? The animal is sold to someone who needs an עולה. The money is non-holy, except for the money paid for that one limb. This is the view of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not agree with רבי יוסי's starting point about an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, only the leg becomes holy. The whole animal is still sold to be brought as an עולה, and only the money for the leg is holy. Since they reject the idea that the leg spreads holiness to the whole animal, רבי יוסי's comparison would not convince them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'one might think', which introduces a wrong first assumption
'the פסוק teaches', which introduces the source that corrects the assumption
non-holy, ordinary
a limb
the money or value paid for something

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows exactly where the two pairs of תנאים disagree: does a leg declaration make the whole animal holy or not? The proof in the next steps depends on this.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
One might think that one who says, 'The leg of this one is a burnt offering,'
all of it will be a burnt offering?
The verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״ –
phrases.english: 'Anything of it that he gives to the Lord shall be holy'
part of it is holy, but not all of it is holy.
One might think it can go out to non-holy status?
phrases.notes: He means the holy leg. Maybe it could be redeemed and become ordinary again.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'It shall be'
it shall stay as it is.
So how does it work?
It is sold for the needs of burnt offerings,
and the money for it is non-holy,
except for the money for the limb in it.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 for רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה: they do not hold that reasoning.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה reject the idea that a leg declaration makes the whole animal an עולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'ממנו' (part of it) from ויקרא 27:9.

steps.title: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say the whole animal becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון learn from 'יהיה' that declaring a leg an עולה makes the whole animal an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: How do we know that if someone says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה,' the whole animal becomes an עולה? The פסוק says 'it shall be,' which includes the whole animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other opinion. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון are the ones who hold that a leg declaration spreads to the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know who accepts רבי יוסי's starting point: רבי יוסי himself and רבי שמעון. Both pairs read the same word 'יהיה' differently. For רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה it means the leg stays holy. For רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון it means the whole animal is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'from where do we know?', which asks for a source
to include, to add something to the law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two subjects up. Here רבי שמעון agrees with רבי יוסי about an עולה. The disagreement between them is only about תמורה, and that is why רבי יוסי can push him with the comparison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
From where do we know that one who says, 'The leg of this one is a burnt offering,'
all of it will be a burnt offering?
The verse teaches: 'It shall be'
to include all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by giving the opposite view to step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a leg declaration makes the whole animal an עולה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ברייתא, reading 'יהיה' as including the whole animal.

steps.title: So רבי יוסי must be arguing with רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה reject the עולה idea, רבי יוסי must be answering רבי שמעון. So 'אין ממירין' is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom is he answering? If רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, do they hold this idea? No. So he must be answering רבי שמעון!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question and draws the conclusion: רבי יוסי's argument only makes sense against רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי argues: 'You agree a leg declaration makes the whole animal an עולה, so agree the same for תמורה.' Only רבי שמעון agrees about the עולה. So the person who says a leg cannot be made a תמורה seems to be רבי שמעון, which would support רב שימי בר אשי's claim. The next step challenges this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'rather, isn't it…?', which introduces the only option left
an animal swapped for a holy animal, which also becomes holy

steps.whatToRemember: The proof assumes רבי יוסי's 'just as with an עולה' argument is a reply to someone who agrees about the עולה, and that would be רבי שמעון. The next step questions that assumption.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the attempted proof asked for in step 5. If it held, it would back רב שימי בר אשי's answer, but step 11 shows it is not decisive.

phrases.english: To whom?
If to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
do they hold this reasoning?
Rather, isn't it to Rabbi Shimon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from steps 8 and 9 to answer the question of step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof suggests רבי יוסי is arguing with רבי שמעון, so 'אין ממירין' would follow רבי שמעון. Step 11 rejects this.

steps.title: רבי יוסי may simply be giving his own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 10. רבי יוסי may not be answering anyone at all; he may just be explaining his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רבי יוסי was stating his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down its own conclusion that the משנה in תמורה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 assumed that רבי יוסי's comparison to עולה must be a reply to some other תנא. Here the גמרא says it doesn't have to be a reply. רבי יוסי could just be giving the reason for his own position. So the proof that 'אין ממירין' is רבי שמעון's view falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: His own reasoning; he is not reacting to someone else
He is saying

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to pin 'אין ממירין' on רבי שמעון ends without a proof, because רבי יוסי may only be explaining himself.

phrases.english: No,
Rabbi Yosei is stating his own reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי טַעְמָא דְנַפְשֵׁיהּ קָאָמַר
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that 'אין ממירין' is the view of רבי שמעון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that רבי יוסי must be answering another תנא, but he may just be explaining his own view

steps.title: A firstborn animal stuck during birth
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a firstborn is stuck in the womb, it may be cut up and thrown to dogs. Once most of it has come out, it is holy, must be buried, and the mother is free from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal giving birth to its firstborn that has trouble giving birth: one may cut the baby up limb by limb and throw it to the dogs. If most of it already came out, it must be buried, and the mother is now exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic about a בכור that gets stuck while being born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור only becomes holy when it is born. While it is still inside, it is ordinary, so it can be cut up and given to dogs. Once most of it is out, it counts as born. It is holy and must be buried, and since the mother has already 'given birth' she cannot have another בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal giving birth for the first time
Having a hard time giving birth
Most of it came out
Must be buried, like any holy animal that cannot be used
The mother is free from בכורה, so her later babies are not בכורות

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that 'most of it out' counts as birth is the starting point for the dispute that comes next.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
An animal giving birth to its firstborn that is having difficulty giving birth:
one may cut up the fetus limb by limb,
and throw it to the dogs.
If most of it came out,
it must be buried,
and the mother is exempt from firstborn status.
phrases.notes: The mother's next babies won't count as בכורות, since this one already counts as her first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before most of the בכור comes out, it is ordinary and may be cut up. Once most of it is out, it is holy, needs burial, and the mother is exempt from future בכורה.

steps.title: Selling a partly-born firstborn to a gentile
steps.stepSummary: A third of the בכור came out, the owner sold it to a גוי, and then another third came out. רב הונא says it is holy; רבה says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a third came out, he sold it to a גוי, and then another third came out. רב הונא says it is holy. רבה says it is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between אמוראים that builds on the משנה's rule that 'most of it out' counts as birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור that belongs to a גוי does not become holy. Here the sale happened after one third was out but before most of it was out. The question is when the holiness takes effect: at the start of the birth, or only when most of it is out.

keyTerms.meaning: One third
And he sold it to a non-Jew
Holy, with בכור status
Not holy

steps.confusionAlert: Two thirds together is 'most', so by the end the animal is born. The whole question is whether the sale in the middle matters.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was stated: if one third came out
and he sold it to a gentile,
and then another third came out:
Rav Huna says: it is holy.
Rabba says: it is not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's 'most of it' rule to a case where the animal was sold in the middle of the birth
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא says the בכור is holy; רבה says it is not.

steps.title: רב הונא: holiness works backwards
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds the בכור becomes holy retroactively from the beginning of the birth, so the sale to the גוי never really happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says it is holy because he holds it becomes holy backwards. Once most of it came out, it became clear that it was holy from the start, so what he sold was nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that once most of the animal is out, its holiness goes back to the moment the first part came out. So at the time of the sale the animal was already holy, and the owner couldn't sell it. The sale is empty, the גוי owns nothing, and the בכור stays holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Backwards in time, retroactively
It became clear (that it was already true)
From the beginning
He sold nothing at all

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of things becoming clear backwards (איגלאי מילתא למפרע) shows up all over ש״ס.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says it is holy:
he holds it is holy retroactively,
and once most of it came out,
it became clear retroactively
that it was holy from the beginning,
phrases.notes: "From the beginning" means from when the first third came out, before the sale.

phrases.english: and what he sold, he sold nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר קָדוֹשׁ: קָסָבַר לְמַפְרֵעַ קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of the first opinion in the dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The holiness of a בכור takes effect backwards, from the moment it starts coming out, so a sale in the middle of the birth does nothing.

steps.title: רבה: the sale to the gentile works, so the firstborn is not holy
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that the בכור is not holy. In his view it only becomes holy from the moment most of it comes out, so the earlier sale to the גוי was valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: it is not holy. He holds it becomes holy only from now on, so what the owner sold, he sold properly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבה's side of the argument from step 13 and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said holiness reaches back to the start of the birth, so the sale never took effect. רבה says holiness only begins once most of the animal is out. When the owner sold the animal after only a third had come out, it was not holy yet, so the sale worked. By the time most of it was out, a גוי partly owned it, and a בכור partly owned by a גוי does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: From now on: the holiness starts only at that moment, not earlier
He sold it properly: the sale was valid
He holds: introduces the reason behind a ruling

phrases.english: Rabba says: it is not holy.
He holds that it becomes holy only from now on,
phrases.notes: "Now" means the moment most of the animal has come out.

phrases.english: and what he sold, he sold properly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the argument, after step 14 explained רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבה, a בכור becomes holy only from the moment most of it comes out. So a sale to a גוי before that point is valid, and the animal is not holy.

steps.title: The same two sages argue in a second case: partly born through the side wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב הונא and רבה are consistent. They also argue about a בכור that came out one third through a cut in the side and two thirds through the womb. רב הונא says not holy, and רבה says holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, as it was stated: if a third came out through the side wall and two thirds through the womb, רב הונא says it is not holy, and רבה says it is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a second argument between the same two אמוראים and says it comes from the same root. Here it only states the case and the rulings. The explanation comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is only holy if it comes out through the opening of the womb. In this case most of the animal did come out through the womb, but the first part came out through a cut in the side. Look carefully: here רב הונא is the one who says not holy, and רבה says holy. That is the opposite of the sale case.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning: each sage is consistent with his view elsewhere
The side wall: a birth through a cut in the mother's side
Womb: here it means the normal opening of the womb
A third

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. In the sale case רב הונא says holy and רבה says not holy. In the side-wall case it is the other way around. Each one still uses the same principle; it just gives different results.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning,
as it was stated:
If a third came out through the side wall,
phrases.notes: This means the mother was cut open, and part of the calf came out through that cut.

phrases.english: and two thirds came out through the womb —
Rav Huna says: it is not holy,
Rabba says: it is holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the argument in steps 13-15 to a second, parallel argument between the same sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a third of a בכור came out through the side and two thirds through the womb, רב הונא says it is not holy and רבה says it is holy.

steps.title: Explaining each side in the side-wall case
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says not holy because holiness goes back to the start, and the first majority did not come out through the womb. רבה says holy because holiness starts now, and most of the animal did come out through the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says it is not holy. He follows his reasoning that it becomes holy retroactively, and the first majority was not in the womb. רבה says it is holy. He follows his reasoning that it becomes holy from now on, and the majority came out through the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how each sage's ruling in the side-wall case comes straight from his general view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the birth "counts" from its very beginning. The first majority to come out included the third that came through the side, so it was not a proper birth through the womb. For רבה, what matters is the moment most of the animal is out through the womb, and two thirds did come out that way, so it is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactively: the holiness reaches back to the start of the birth
The first majority: the first time more than half of the animal was out
It is not (there)
Came out

steps.whatToRemember: One principle, two cases. רב הונא: holiness goes back to the start (לְמַפְרֵעַ). רבה: holiness starts only when most of it is out (מִכָּאן וּלְהַבָּא).

phrases.english: Rav Huna says: it is not holy.
Rav Huna follows his own reasoning, as he said:
it becomes holy retroactively,
and the first majority was not in the womb.
phrases.notes: The first time more than half was out, that half included the third that came through the side.

phrases.english: Rabba says: it is holy.
Rabba follows his own reasoning, as he said:
it becomes holy from now on,
and the majority came out through the womb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the rulings stated in step 16 using the principles from steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: not holy, because holiness goes back to the start and the first majority was not through the womb. רבה: holy, because holiness starts now and most of it came out through the womb.

steps.title: Why both cases are needed: the first half of the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain why we need the argument in both cases. If we had only the sale case, we might think רב הונא only holds his view there, because רבה's view would lead to a leniency. In the side-wall case, where רבה's view is the strict one, we might think רב הונא agrees with רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to teach both. If we had only been taught this case, we would say רב הונא says his view here because the other view leads to a leniency. But in that case, where the other view leads to a stringency, I would say he agrees with רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a צריכותא, an explanation of why both cases had to be taught. This is the first half. The other half, explaining why the side-wall case alone would not be enough, comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the sale case, רבה's view makes the animal not holy, which is a leniency. So maybe רב הונא only rejects רבה there, to avoid being lenient. In the side-wall case, רבה's view makes the animal holy, which is the strict side. So maybe רב הונא would agree with רבה there. Teaching the side-wall case shows that רב הונא holds his view even when it leads to the lenient result.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: the גמרא explains why two cases that seem the same both had to be taught
Toward leniency
Toward strictness
Agrees, concedes

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if we had been taught only this case,
phrases.notes: "This case" is the one where a third came out and was sold to a גוי.

phrases.english: we would say that in this case Rav Huna says his view
because the other view leads to a leniency,
phrases.notes: He means רבה's view, which would free the animal from being a בכור.

phrases.english: but in that case, where it leads to strictness —
phrases.notes: "That case" is the side-wall case, where רבה's view makes the animal holy.

phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Rabba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing the two parallel arguments, the גמרא explains why both had to be recorded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sale case alone would not be enough. We might think רב הונא's view there only comes from avoiding a leniency, and that in the side-wall case, where רבה is the strict one, רב הונא would agree with him.
steps.whyThisMatters: A צריכותא shows that each case teaches something new. Here it shows that each sage's view is a real principle about when holiness starts, not just a choice to be strict or lenient.
